name: Albescent-Dolmen
description: Glacier upon glacier, blue-white and creaking, buried in places by nitrogen snow. The shell is broken in places by frozen methane lakes, and through those breaches the deep ocean breathes plumes of frost into the dark.
There is a hush that is not emptiness but attention, as if the landscape were listening back. Visitors report dreams of falling that persist for days after departure.
Local legend among spacers says the planet hums on a frequency just below hearing. Instruments confirm it. Nobody agrees on the source.
For traders, water and dark crystals alone justifies the crossing; for everyone else, the planet pays in questions. Fuel is cheap, information is not, and both are dangerous to carry.
